**DN02** is a medical diagnosis code representing recurrent and persistent blood in the urine. Within the Danish healthcare system, it is utilized as a specific tracking metric by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) to monitor patient outcomes and clinical quality.

Specifically, DN02 is a component of the clinical quality indicators for [[atrieflimren]]. It is used to calculate the incidence of severe bleeding events among patients treated for this condition [^src1]. Because patients with atrial fibrillation are frequently prescribed anticoagulants, tracking severe bleeding is a critical safety and quality measure. DN02 is grouped alongside other codes such as [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]] to capture urinary and respiratory tract bleeding, complementing broader diagnostic categories for intracranial (e.g., [[di60|DI60]]) and gastrointestinal bleeding (e.g., [[dk25-0|DK25.0]]) [^src1]. 

The code appears in the technical methodology and definition sections of the annual reports for the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database, serving as a standardized reference for data collection, denominator/numerator calculations, and regional comparison across the Danish healthcare system [^src1] [^src2].
